To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the admission of learners into ITE institutions in Eritrea is influenced by the following factors: (a) the prevailing stereotypes around teaching profession; (b) the admission process; (c) the institutional factors; and (d) the systemic factors; and (2) the prevailing stereotypes and admission process have a negative impact on learners’ learning process in the College of education.

the nature of the admission to the CoE, the stereotypes around the teaching and teacher education profession, and the nature of the learning process in the College of education are the major stumbling blocks that affect the classroom practices at the College and beyond.

(1) prospective teachers are not admitted to the CoE based on their interest and commitment to teaching; (2) the prevailing stereotyped views around the teaching profession and ITE institutions are a major obstacle for the provision of quality teaching in the CoE; and (3) the admission process of prospective teachers to ITE institutions and the stereotyper views around the profession need to be reexamined in order to ensure that prospective teachers are well prepared to face the challenges in the teaching profession.

the admission process of the prospective teachers in the college of education.

the admission process of prospective teachers to the College of Education, the nature of teaching as a profession in the country and the stereotypes surrounding the teaching profession are the major stumbling blocks that affect the quality of teacher education in the college.

the teaching profession is not only about teaching, it is a social practice that is influenced by a number of social factors.
the admission process and the stereotyping of the teaching profession in the public domain are among the major factors that affect the quality of the teaching profession at the CoE and beyond.
the teaching profession in Eritrea is not only in a dire need of a re-branding, but also a re-structuring of the admission process of prospective teachers into the college.
